topic_title: Mission, Scope, and KPIs of a SOC
topic_summary: What a SOC actually delivers to the business and how its effectiveness is measured.

flashcards.front: State the SOC mission in one sentence.
flashcards.back: Continuously detect, analyze, and respond to cybersecurity events that threaten the organization's assets and operations.
Mean Time To Detect — the average elapsed time between an incident's onset and the SOC noticing it.
Mean Time To Respond — average elapsed time between detection and the start of effective response actions.

flashcards.front: Why is alert volume a *misleading* KPI on its own?
flashcards.back: High volume can simply mean noisy rules; without precision/recall context it doesn't measure security outcomes.

flashcards.front: What's the difference between in-house and outsourced (MSSP) SOCs in two bullet points?
flashcards.back: In-house: full context, slower to staff, expensive. MSSP: faster to spin up and 24×7 coverage, but limited business context and shared analysts.

questions.stem: Which metric most directly reflects how quickly a SOC notices that something is wrong?
questions.explanation: MTTD measures time from incident start to detection. MTTR measures time from detection to response.

questions.stem: A SOC reports 'alert volume rose 300% this quarter.' What is the single most important follow-up question?

options.label: A
options.content: How many of those were true positives?

options.label: B
options.content: How many analysts do we have?

questions.explanation: Without the true-positive ratio, alert volume tells you about noise, not security posture.

questions.stem: Pick two reasons an organization might choose an MSSP over building in-house.

options.label: B
options.content: Lower per-analyst cost at small scale

questions.explanation: MSSPs win on time-to-coverage and shared cost. In-house SOCs retain context and detection-content ownership.
